patch_description: Replace the single-sample greedy with a beam search over transaction orderings. Each beam state holds a partial sequence and its cost; at each step we expand every state with all remaining transactions, evaluate with `get_opt_seq_cost`, and keep the best `beam_width` states. Beam search directly optimizes actual makespan (not proxies like length/write-count), corrects greedy mistakes by keeping several candidates alive, and is far more sample-efficient than random restarts of a 1-sample greedy. Depth-adaptive width: wide (e.g. 10-12) early where branching error compounds most, narrowing (3-4) later to keep runtime bounded. We also run a few restarts with different initial transactions to add diversity, keeping the best overall schedule.
